cultural.vision_reason: This is a carved and painted wooden feast dish in human form with Northwest Coast-style facial painting (ovoid/U-forms), a form and style consistent with Haida (or closely related Northwest Coast) carving traditions, though the museum's own text notes it as wood, not ceramic. The object clearly reflects something the Haida made and used, so it belongs despite the miscategorization.

physical.title: dish; souvenir
physical.summary: Dish, carved in alder wood?, in the form of a human on hands and knees, the head swivelled round to face over the left shoulder. The bowl shape is roughly oval, shallow carved, with three dimensional arms, legs and head. The whole is painted red, with hands feet and rim edge, in green, the hair, eyebrows and pupils in black, the nostrils and mouth in red, the face around the eyes extensively painted in green with 'U' forms. Traditionally assumed to be a woman, no doubt because of the pose and some simple indication of incised genitalia, there is a note, probably from his 1976 visit, saying 'Male. B Holm.' The bowl is unused.
